__baseline_prompt__.text: A palace court costume photograph of a woman portrayed as the portrait subject in a still moment in a palace court. Build a contemporary staged reconstruction of a late Qing Chinese palace corridor: she has reached a half-open vermilion doorway and is waiting to enter, her body facing the opening while her face turns gently back toward the camera. Use the supplied photograph as the face-and-hair appearance reference, preserving its facial proportions, dark eyes, short glossy dark bob and fine separated fringe. Her clothing and the palace are newly staged for this photograph. A long patterned silk court robe falls in a single vertical mass, its sleeves broad enough to produce a weighty fold at each wrist. She holds one closed rectangular silk document folio horizontally at her waist, both palms supporting its underside, elbows comfortably bent with each hand emerging from its own sleeve. The visible folio and her pause at the open threshold suggest an interrupted audience rather than a costume display. Her composed mouth and attentive eyes create a quiet personal presence, while a soft gleam on the cheek and silk supports a subtle, intimate attraction. Deep red door frames repeat behind her and converge toward the dim hall; a strip of cool courtyard daylight crosses the threshold and the front edge of her robe. Frame from head to just below the knees with the face, both hands and the whole folio readable together, an eye-level three-quarter view with natural perspective. Keep the near sleeve folds and skin texture tactile, the far corridor gently softened, and the costume's form clear enough to inspect. Photograph the real-looking set with restrained warm reds, deep blue-green silk and cool natural light.
